We further show that DS-constrained stream mixing does not increase the differential entropy of the transmitted features. This implies no increase in the ideal EB coding length. Experiments on SemCom and TOC under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN), Rayleigh fading, Rician fading, and imperfect channel state information (CSI) show that the proposed scheme improves semantic/task performance, communication robustness, and convergence stability over residual and unconstrained HC baselines, while requiring no additional channel uses.
tldr: This paper proposes a manifold-constrained hyper-connection coding scheme with entropy bottleneck for resource-efficient semantic and task-oriented communication over wireless channels.
motivation: Semantic communication aims to reduce wireless resource consumption by transmitting only task-relevant information, but existing methods often increase complexity and channel uses to improve reliability. The authors aim to balance performance and resource usage with explicit rate control.
method: The proposed mHC-based semantic encoder uses multiple residual streams constrained by doubly stochastic mixing matrices, and an entropy bottleneck quantizes channel features to estimate the entropy-coded rate, enabling end-to-end rate-distortion/task optimization under bandwidth and power constraints.
result: Experiments under various channel conditions show improved semantic/task performance, robustness, and convergence stability over baselines, with no additional channel uses and negligible overhead.
conclusion: The mHC coding scheme offers a resource-efficient approach for semantic communication, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: EM-Guided Graph Learning For Fluid Antenna Beamforming Under Current-Domain Constraints
authors: Yuanhui Wu, Hao Jiang, Zaichen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid antenna arrays (FAAs) reconfigure a finite set of radiating ports within a prescribed aperture. In compact apertures, however, channel-driven placement may cluster ports, strengthen mutual coupling, degrade radiation conditioning, increase source-voltage demand, and produce uneven current loading. This paper studies downlink multi-user beamforming with jointly optimized port placement and current-domain transmission. An electromagnetic-guided graph network predicts port layouts from channel observations and refines them using geometric and mutual-impedance information. The training objective jointly considers communication performance and electromagnetic feasibility, while a common evaluation procedure is applied to all methods. The results show that, under a common feasibility standard, the proposed method provides a controllable tradeoff among communication rate, current loading, and configuration latency.
tldr: This paper proposes an electromagnetic-guided graph learning method for fluid antenna beamforming, focusing on port placement and current-domain constraints.
motivation: To address performance degradation in compact fluid antenna arrays due to mutual coupling and uneven current loading, by jointly optimizing port placement and transmission.
method: Uses a graph neural network to predict port layouts from channel observations, refined with geometric and mutual-impedance information, and trained with a joint objective considering communication performance and electromagnetic feasibility.
result: Under a common feasibility standard, the method provides a controllable tradeoff among communication rate, current loading, and configuration latency.
conclusion: The proposed approach effectively balances communication and electromagnetic constraints, offering a practical solution for fluid antenna beamforming.

title: MiLAC-Aided Beamforming For Mimo Over-the-Air Computation
authors: Yaru Wang, Deyou Zhang, Qingchao Li, Jun Liu, Chuang Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) enables low-latency wireless data aggregation, but its accuracy is limited by imperfect signal alignment over fading channels and receiver noise. Fully digital beamforming improves aggregation accuracy in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) AirComp systems but requires one radio-frequency (RF) chain per antenna. To reduce this hardware burden, we investigate microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC)-aided beamforming for MIMO AirComp. Under a lossless and reciprocal MiLAC model, we jointly optimize the transmit digital precoding matrices and the receive-side MiLAC aggregation matrix to minimize the mean squared error (MSE). An alternating optimization algorithm is developed, in which the precoding matrices are optimally updated using the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions and bisection, while the resulting convex aggregation matrix subproblem is solved globally using projected gradient descent. Numerical results verify the algorithm's convergence and demonstrate that MiLAC-aided beamforming approaches the MSE performance of fully digital beamforming with substantially fewer RF chains and outperforms phase-shifter-based hybrid beamforming under the same RF-chain budget.
tldr: This paper proposes a MiLAC-aided beamforming scheme for MIMO over-the-air computation to reduce RF chains while maintaining aggregation accuracy.
motivation: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) suffers from signal misalignment and noise, and fully digital beamforming requires many RF chains, which is hardware-intensive.
method: The authors jointly optimize transmit digital precoding and receive MiLAC aggregation matrix to minimize MSE, using alternating optimization with KKT conditions and projected gradient descent.
result: Numerical results show MiLAC-aided beamforming approaches fully digital performance with fewer RF chains and outperforms phase-shifter-based hybrid beamforming.
conclusion: MiLAC-aided beamforming offers a hardware-efficient solution for MIMO AirComp, balancing performance and complexity.

abstract:

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.

method: The review discusses the principles of tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy, where a scanning tip acts as an optical antenna to confine light and achieve superresolution.
result: The technique enables atomic-scale spatial resolution in fluorescence imaging, revealing electronic and vibronic properties of molecules.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for nanoscale imaging, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices, so understanding its mechanisms is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize recent experimental and simulation studies to propose a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation, involving surface defects, field emission, heating, and plasma formation.
result: They identify key interacting factors that trigger breakdown and suggest how these insights can guide improvements in high-power technologies.
conclusion: A unified understanding of vacuum breakdown can lead to more reliable and efficient accelerators and other high-field devices.

The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications, including magnetism, topology, and dynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize the rapidly evolving field of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials, which has challenged theories and opened new applications.
method: It is a review article that synthesizes current knowledge on magnetic phenomena, including experimental and theoretical advances.
result: The review highlights new phenomena such as topological magnetism, nonequilibrium dynamics, and interactions with light and electric fields.
conclusion: The field is expanding theoretical understanding and materials capabilities, with promising directions for applications.

authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, discussing electronic structure, correlation effects, and observed phenomena.
result: The review highlights the rich physics of kagome metals, including topological flat bands, Dirac fermions, and various ordered states, but does not present new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: Kagome metals serve as a platform for exploring strongly correlated and topological physics, but the paper is a review and not directly aligned with the user's research interests.

Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for chemical, ecological, and epidemiological modeling.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for analyzing complex systems modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, which are prevalent in biology, sociology, and traffic flow.
method: The review presents field-theoretic techniques, including path integrals and quantum operator methods, to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The paper demonstrates how diverse models can be unified under a single field-theoretic framework, offering a comprehensive pedagogical overview.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond chemistry, but the work is a review without novel contributions to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes how neutron star observations constrain the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: Understanding the equation of state of dense matter is crucial for nuclear physics and astrophysics, and neutron stars provide a unique laboratory.
method: The paper reviews recent observational results from binary neutron star mergers (gravitational waves) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, and compares them to theoretical predictions from nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and the comparison with theoretical predictions helps discriminate among different equation of state models.
conclusion: Current observations are beginning to constrain the dense matter equation of state, and future observations will further improve our understanding.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research, emphasizing the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes findings from experiments, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations in spin-glass systems.
result: It tracks progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and highlights future research opportunities.
conclusion: The review underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration in advancing spin-glass physics.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic states of matter with potential applications in quantum computing, but their realization in materials is challenging.
method: The review summarizes theoretical models (Kitaev model) and experimental progress on candidate materials, emphasizing chiral edge modes.
result: The review highlights leading candidate materials and their topological properties, providing a comprehensive overview.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are promising but require further experimental and theoretical work to confirm and utilize their properties.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review connects statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to large-scale neural recordings, but it is not aligned with the specified research directions.
motivation: The authors aim to bridge statistical physics and neuroscience to uncover reproducible behaviors in neural networks.
method: The paper reviews recent progress, discussing maximum entropy models and renormalization group approaches applied to multi-neuron recordings.
result: It highlights that statistical physics models can provide predictive power for neural activity, revealing new reproducible behaviors.
conclusion: The review argues that abstract theoretical principles from physics can be effectively applied to brain studies, but it does not contribute to the user's focus areas.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on photophysical processes.

method: The paper reviews various theoretical approaches to describe nonradiative transitions in quantum systems.
result: Summarizes the state of the art and identifies potential applications.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To provide an overview of quantum properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics and quantum technologies.
method: A review article summarizing theoretical and experimental work on quantum interactions underlying skyrmion formation and quantum characteristics of skyrmions.
result: The paper discusses quantum aspects such as quantum fluctuations, tunneling, and entanglement in skyrmion systems, and their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit quantum properties that could be harnessed for future quantum technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers atomic-scale microscopy techniques for measuring disorder in semiconductors, which is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to review real-space techniques for characterizing atomic-scale disorder in compound semiconductors, which is important for material properties but not directly related to the user's focus areas.
method: The review discusses three real-space techniques: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, and their combined use for measuring disorder.
result: The paper provides an overview of how these techniques can be applied to semiconductors, emphasizing cases where they are combined for a more complete picture of defects.
conclusion: The review concludes that these microscopy techniques are valuable for understanding disorder in semiconductors, but the topic is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, potentially mediated by exotic bosons and related to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To summarize the state of the art in searches for new spin-dependent forces, which could reveal physics beyond the Standard Model and shed light on dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper is a review, compiling theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizing experimental constraints from various precision measurement techniques.
result: The review consolidates current knowledge and experimental limits on spin-dependent exotic interactions, highlighting the most stringent constraints and future prospects.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, with ongoing and future experiments expected to improve sensitivity.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of nuclear reaction theory relevant to stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, addressing the challenge of measuring low-energy reactions in the lab.
method: It reviews theoretical approaches for low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses new experimental ideas.
result: The review consolidates the state of the art in stellar nuclear reaction theory and highlights novel methods for studying these reactions on Earth.
conclusion: The paper is a valuable resource for nuclear astrophysics but does not contribute to the user's research directions in quantum information science.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining that apparent violations arise from violating assumptions in the bounds' derivations.
motivation: To clarify why some measured material properties exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how designing materials to violate these assumptions can lead to interesting properties.
method: A review of various circumstances where measurements exceed thermodynamic bounds, analyzing which underlying assumptions are violated in each case.
result: Identifies multiple examples across fields where apparent violations occur and explains the specific assumptions that are not met.
conclusion: Understanding and intentionally violating the assumptions behind thermodynamic bounds can enable the development of materials with unusual properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology, potentially offering new platforms for quantum simulation.
method: The paper surveys various atomic, photonic, and electronic systems used to realize these geometries, discussing theoretical models and experimental techniques.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current progress and challenges in simulating quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries.
conclusion: The field is promising for advancing quantum simulation, but the paper is a review without novel technical contributions directly aligned with the user's specific research directions.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This review covers nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses a classical mechanics phenomenon in soft matter, which is outside the specified research interests.
method: It integrates bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and integral techniques to analyze the Biot instability.
result: Provides a modern treatment of nonlinear elasticity for soft matter buckling.

title: Entropic Collapse And Extreme First-passage Times In Discrete Ballistic Transport
authors: Bhargav R Karamched
abstract: We investigate the extreme first-passage statistics of non-interacting random walkers on hierarchical ballistic graphs. By distinguishing between transport limited by escape from localized initial states (injection-limited) and transport limited by the extended network (bulk-limited), we identify a class of extreme value statistics that arises in geometries dominated by source traps (e.g. the Comet graph). In this regime, the distribution of the minimum arrival time does not converge to any of the classical generalized extreme value distributions. Instead, it follows a discrete distribution with a strict lower time bound determined by the properties of the hierarchical network. We analytically derive the asymptotic behavior of this class and validate our predictions against Monte Carlo simulations. Crucially, we identify the mechanism of ‘entropic collapse’ that destroys this scaling in bulk-dominated geometries like the Bethe lattice, where the phase space of delayed paths diverges with distance. This work establishes a geometry-encoding function that acts as a diagnostic tool for ascertaining whether or not a given graph is hierarchical.
tldr: This paper studies extreme first-passage statistics of random walkers on hierarchical graphs, identifying a new class of extreme value statistics and the mechanism of 'entropic collapse'.
motivation: To understand extreme first-passage times in complex networks, which is relevant to transport phenomena but not directly to the user's research interests.
method: Analytical derivations and Monte Carlo simulations for random walks on hierarchical ballistic graphs, distinguishing injection-limited and bulk-limited transport.
result: Identifies a discrete distribution for minimum arrival times in source-trap geometries, and shows that 'entropic collapse' destroys this scaling in bulk-dominated geometries.
conclusion: Establishes a geometry-encoding function to diagnose hierarchical graphs, but the topic is outside the specified research directions.

title: Dimensionality And Confinement Reshape Competition In Cellular Renewing Active Matter
authors: Philip Bittihn And Yoav G Pollack Patrick Zimmer
abstract: Cellular renewing active matter—assemblies of proliferating and apoptotic cells—underlies tissue homeostasis, morphogenesis, and clonal competition. Previous work in one-dimensional periodic systems identified a fitness advantage associated with rapid dead-cell clearance, an ‘opportunistic’ competition mechanism. Extending this framework, we study two-dimensional cellular aggregates and show that dimensionality modifies the interplay between competition mechanisms for clones with different clearance rates: in 2D, opportunistic and homeostatic-pressure-based competition jointly shape clonal selection, to varying degrees. We then introduce an explicit circular confinement to probe how physical boundaries modulate this interplay. While opportunistic competition persists, distinct time-dependent behaviors emerge through weakened homeostatic-pressure-based competition near boundaries. Structural analysis reveals that confinement promotes tangential alignment and spatially heterogeneous homeostatic pressure, thereby reshaping competitive outcomes at tissue edges. Partial information decomposition allows us to attribute these differing outcomes to temporally and spatially varying relative contributions of the two mechanisms. Our study connects newly discovered competition mechanisms with more realistic biological contexts, highlighting how dimensionality and spatial constraints influence tissue structures and modulate competition in heterogeneous cell populations across time and space, with implications for tumor growth dynamics and tissue development.
tldr: This paper studies cellular renewing active matter in 2D with confinement, focusing on competition mechanisms between clones with different clearance rates.
motivation: To extend previous 1D findings on 'opportunistic' competition to more realistic 2D and confined geometries, relevant to tissue homeostasis and tumor growth.
method: They use computational modeling of cellular aggregates, structural analysis, and partial information decomposition to quantify the contributions of competition mechanisms.
result: Dimensionality and confinement alter the interplay between opportunistic and homeostatic-pressure-based competition, with boundary effects leading to spatially heterogeneous outcomes.
conclusion: The study highlights how physical constraints modulate clonal competition, with implications for tissue development and tumor dynamics.

title: Excitons In 2H-MoTe2: Anisotropies, Masses And Binding Energy
authors: Zahra Ahmadi Heidari And Martin Knupfer
abstract: Bound electron–hole pairs called excitons determine the photophysical behavior of semiconducting materials. In this study, we present a combination of electron energy-loss spectroscopy in transmission and optical absorption spectroscopy for the investigation of excitons in bulk 2H-MoTe2. The exciton dispersion E(q) was measured for momentum transfers oriented along the ΓK and ΓM directions at 20 K. From the extracted dispersion relations, the in-plane exciton effective mass was determined. Our results reveal that for 2H-MoTe2 the exciton effective mass is anisotropic. In consideration of the complementary optical results the exciton reduced mass, binding energy and radius have been determined.
tldr: This paper studies exciton properties in bulk 2H-MoTe2 using electron energy-loss and optical absorption spectroscopy, focusing on anisotropic effective masses and binding energy.
motivation: Understanding exciton behavior in transition metal dichalcogenides is important for optoelectronic applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors combine electron energy-loss spectroscopy in transmission and optical absorption spectroscopy to measure exciton dispersion along ΓK and ΓM directions at 20 K, extracting effective masses and binding energy.
result: The exciton effective mass is anisotropic, and the reduced mass, binding energy, and radius are determined from complementary optical results.
conclusion: The study provides detailed exciton parameters for 2H-MoTe2, but it is purely a condensed matter physics investigation without relevance to the user's research directions.

title: Low-dimensional Dynamical Behavior Of Locally Coupled Chiral Swarmalators
authors: Zihan Li, Yonggang Wu, Xiaoyu Zhang, Zhigang Zheng And Duxin Chen
abstract: Understanding the dynamical behavior of swarmalators, particularly the transition from disorder to synchronization, constitutes one of the pivotal frontiers in the study of complex systems. We propose an ansatz that successfully decouples the spatial and phase dynamics in the locally coupled chiral swarmalators model, enabling rigorous analytical treatment of this complex system. Within this framework, we systematically examine how the interaction radius affects system synchronization, quantified through an order parameter measuring phase coherence. Our theoretical analysis reveals that increasing the interaction radius enhances synchronization in both velocity and phase dynamics. This relationship demonstrates that larger interaction networks facilitate more efficient information transfer among heterogeneous oscillators with different intrinsic frequencies. Using a self-consistent approach in the thermodynamic limit, we derive analytical expressions for the order parameter that accurately predict the synchronization transition. These findings provide fundamental insights into synchronization mechanisms in spatially embedded swarmalator systems with applications in understanding biological collective behaviors.
tldr: This paper analyzes synchronization in a model of chiral swarmalators with local coupling, deriving analytical expressions for the order parameter.
motivation: Understanding synchronization in swarmalator systems is important for biological collective behaviors, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors propose an ansatz to decouple spatial and phase dynamics, then use a self-consistent approach in the thermodynamic limit to derive analytical expressions for the order parameter.
result: They find that increasing the interaction radius enhances synchronization in both velocity and phase dynamics, and their analytical predictions match the synchronization transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into synchronization in spatially embedded swarmalator systems, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: The Paradox Of Steady-state Light Diffusion
authors: André Liemert, Lorenzo Pattelli, Alwin Kienle, Federico Tommasi And Fabrizio Martelli
abstract: For over thirty years, the definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport has been the subject of persistent debate. Its canonical expression includes an explicit dependence on absorption, violating a fundamental scaling property of the radiative transfer equation (RTE). In the time domain (TD), evidence shows that the correct definition is independent of absorption, yet absorption-dependent formulations unfortunately remain common in practical data analysis. In the continuous-wave regime, the radial decay of the RTE can be reproduced by an absorption-dependent coefficient, but this does not imply that steady-state transport is genuinely diffusive. Here, this controversy is resolved through an exact consistency test based solely on the requirement that diffusion converges to the RTE in the limit of infinite propagation. In the TD, we prove that the absorption-independent coefficient is both necessary and sufficient for exact long-time convergence. In the continuous-wave regime, we prove analytically that no scalar diffusion coefficient can make diffusion asymptotically equivalent to the RTE when absorption is nonzero: matching the dominant attenuation length fixes one coefficient, whereas matching the residue requires a different one. We further show that this failure is not caused by any finite set of ballistic or few-scattering contributions, and quantify the intrinsic error introduced by incorrect parameterizations in idealized absorption-retrieval scenarios. These results establish the time-domain formulation as the only self-consistent reference and call for a re-examination of how diffusion is applied in optical transport studies.
tldr: This paper resolves the long-standing debate on the definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport, proving that in steady-state with absorption no scalar diffusion coefficient can asymptotically match the radiative transfer equation.
motivation: The definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport has been debated for decades, with absorption-dependent formulations violating fundamental scaling properties. The authors aim to resolve this controversy through an exact consistency test.
method: The authors use an exact consistency test based on the requirement that diffusion converges to the radiative transfer equation (RTE) in the limit of infinite propagation. They analytically prove the necessity and sufficiency of an absorption-independent coefficient in the time domain, and show that in the continuous-wave regime no scalar diffusion coefficient can achieve asymptotic equivalence when absorption is nonzero.
result: In the time domain, the absorption-independent coefficient is both necessary and sufficient for exact long-time convergence. In the continuous-wave regime, matching the dominant attenuation length and the residue require different coefficients, proving that no scalar diffusion coefficient can make diffusion asymptotically equivalent to the RTE with absorption.
conclusion: The time-domain formulation is the only self-consistent reference for diffusion in optical transport, and the paper calls for re-examination of how diffusion is applied in studies with absorption.

title: Emergent Symmetry-protected Topological Phases Via Polyakov Confinement In Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Shun-Li Yu And Jian-Xin Li Li-Wei He
abstract: A main theme in modern condensed matter physics is the emergence of fractionalized excitations and gauge structures from quantum spin systems. However, understanding how these exotic degrees of freedom reconfine into new phases of matter remains a fundamental challenge. In this work, we demonstrate that Polyakov’s confinement mechanism-a foundation of compact gauge theory-can serve as a dynamical engine to transform a Dirac spin liquid (DSL) into a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) state. Starting with a DSL with spin-dependent gauge fluxes, we show that the single-occupancy constraint inherent to the physical Hilbert space triggers monopole condensation, dynamically confining bulk spinons while preserving gapless edge modes-realizing a spinon analog of the quantum spin Hall effect. Using a large-scale variational Monte Carlo simulation on a triangular antiferromagnet with an additional Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, we provide microscopic evidence for this confined SPT phase, including a characteristic area law for the Wilson loop and vanishing topological entanglement entropy. Furthermore, we identify a measurable spin-pump response under magnetic fields, which directly encodes the Berry curvature of the parent Dirac cones. Our results reveal a previously unexplored pathway to SPT physics, bridging the fields of gauge theory, quantum magnetism, and topological matter.
tldr: This paper uses Polyakov confinement to transform a Dirac spin liquid into a symmetry-protected topological state, focusing on condensed matter physics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how fractionalized excitations reconfine into new phases, bridging gauge theory and quantum magnetism.
method: They employ large-scale variational Monte Carlo simulations on a triangular antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.
result: They find evidence for a confined SPT phase with area law Wilson loop and vanishing topological entanglement entropy, plus a spin-pump response.
conclusion: The work reveals a new pathway to SPT physics but is primarily a condensed matter study without direct quantum information or thermodynamics focus.

title: Tailoring Reflectionless Complex Media For non-Abelian Braiding Of Acoustic Modes
authors: Hongkuan Zhang And Guancong Ma
abstract: Multiple scattering of sound and light can be tailored for diverse applications. Despite the great progress enabled by technologies such as time-reversal propagation and wavefront shaping, the full control of the transmission matrix remains a significant challenge. In this work, we propose a multi-scattering-based approach to design reflectionless complex media with an arbitrary unitary transmission matrix. As such, the perfect transmission of waves through such a medium performs a unitary operation. Based on this principle, we experimentally demonstrated braiding of multiple waveguide modes in an acoustic waveguide via multiple scattering and showed non-Abelian characteristics arising from the concatenation of distinct complex media. Furthermore, we show that the principle can be extended for realizing arbitrary unitary operations beyond braiding. Our scheme uses generalized Wigner–Smith operators to design the optimal acoustic complex media with near-arbitrary targeted functionalities. The scheme is generally applicable beyond acoustics, with broad implications to other wave types. Our results demonstrate unprecedented control over multiple-scattering waves and establish complex media as a viable route to modal control and operations on compact platforms, providing a new design paradigm for multimode, reconfigurable wave-based devices with potential applications in multiplexed communication, imaging, and the manipulation of quantum waves.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to design reflectionless complex media for arbitrary unitary transmission matrices, experimentally demonstrating non-Abelian braiding of acoustic modes.
motivation: To achieve full control of the transmission matrix in complex media, enabling arbitrary unitary operations for wave-based devices.
method: The authors use generalized Wigner-Smith operators to design acoustic complex media that achieve perfect transmission with a desired unitary transmission matrix, and experimentally implement braiding of waveguide modes.
result: They experimentally demonstrate non-Abelian braiding of multiple waveguide modes in an acoustic waveguide, showing that concatenation of distinct media yields non-Abelian characteristics.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new paradigm for modal control and operations on compact platforms, with potential applications in multiplexed communication, imaging, and manipulation of quantum waves.

title: Moiré-driven Skyrmion Family
authors: Kuan He, Meng-Han Li, Shi-Da Fan, Zi-Bin Lin, Xiao-Ying Zhuang, Cheng-Lin Han, Li-Qun Chen, Zhao-Dong Xu, Xue-Feng Zhu And Tian-Zhi Yang
abstract: Skyrmion family members, including skyrmions, merons, and skyrmioniums, have been observed in diverse physical systems, yet their coexistence and transformation within a single controllable platform remain challenging. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a bilayer twisted moiré elastic system that enables the generation of multiple skyrmion family members with different topological charges. By constructing three-dimensional displacement vector fields, we establish a framework describing the evolution of topological invariants under twist-induced symmetry modulation, thereby governing controlled transitions and the stable coexistence of different skyrmion textures. In addition, manipulating the Lamb-wave phase introduces discontinuous transport of the topological textures, thereby revealing phason-like dynamics within the quasiperiodic structure. Together, these results provide a versatile route for controlling topological textures and open new possibilities for the design of integrated topological wave devices.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a moiré-driven elastic system that generates and controls skyrmion family members, focusing on topological textures in mechanical metamaterials.
motivation: The authors aim to achieve coexistence and transformation of multiple skyrmion family members in a single controllable platform, which has been challenging in diverse physical systems.
method: They construct a bilayer twisted moiré elastic system and use three-dimensional displacement vector fields to describe topological invariant evolution under twist-induced symmetry modulation, also manipulating Lamb-wave phase for discontinuous transport.
result: They experimentally demonstrate generation of multiple skyrmion family members with different topological charges and controlled transitions, revealing phason-like dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a versatile route for controlling topological textures and opens possibilities for integrated topological wave devices.

title: Probing Quark Electromagnetic Properties Via Entangled Quark Pairs In Fragmentation Hadrons At Lepton Colliders
authors: Qing-Hong Cao, Guanghui Li, Xin-Kai Wen And Bin Yan
abstract: Electromagnetic dipole interactions of light quarks induce distinct spin correlations in quark pairs produced at lepton colliders, favoring entangled spin-triplet state aligned along the axis or spin-singlet state. These correlations lead to unique azimuthal asymmetries in inclusive -dihadron pair production and in back-to-back hadron pairs ( ), which are absent in the SM. Using published Belle and BaBar measurements together with projected sensitivities based on ratios of azimuthal asymmetries, we demonstrate that these measurements provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings, with a reduced dependence on poorly known nonperturbative fragmentation functions and free from contamination by other new physics effects. This approach offers a clean and novel probe of light-quark dipole interactions in collider experiments.
tldr: This paper proposes using spin correlations in entangled quark pairs produced at lepton colliders to probe light-quark electromagnetic dipole moments, with constraints from Belle and BaBar data.
motivation: The study aims to provide a clean and novel probe of light-quark dipole interactions, which are poorly constrained and could indicate new physics.
method: The authors analyze spin correlations in quark pairs, focusing on azimuthal asymmetries in inclusive dihadron and back-to-back hadron pair production, and use published Belle/BaBar data plus projected sensitivities to constrain dipole couplings.
result: The measurements provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings with reduced dependence on fragmentation functions and no contamination from other new physics.
conclusion: This approach offers a novel and clean probe of light-quark dipole interactions in collider experiments.

title: El Agente Cuántico: Automating Quantum Simulations
authors: Ignacio Gustin, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Juan B Pérez-Sánchez, Chris Crebolder, Jérôme F Gonthier, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Yuma Nakamura, Karthik Panicker, Manav Ramprasad, Aiwei Yin, Zijian Zhang, Yunheng Zou, Varinia Bernales And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract: Quantum simulation is central to understanding and designing quantum systems across physics and chemistry. However, its practical use is often limited by the exponential growth of Hilbert space and by the increasing complexity of modern quantum-simulation software. Here we introduce El Agente Cuántico, a multi-agent AI system that automates quantum-simulation workflows by translating natural-language scientific intent into executed and validated computations across heterogeneous quantum-software frameworks. By reasoning directly over library documentation and APIs, our agentic system dynamically assembles end-to-end simulations spanning—but not limited to—state preparation, closed- and open-system dynamics, tensor-network methods, quantum control, quantum error correction, and quantum resource estimation. The developed system unifies traditionally distinct simulation paradigms behind a single natural-language interface. Beyond reducing technical barriers, this approach opens a path toward scalable, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous quantum simulation, enabling faster exploration of physical models, rapid hypothesis testing, and closer integration between theory, simulation, and emerging quantum hardware.
tldr: This paper introduces a multi-agent AI system that automates quantum simulation workflows via natural language, but it does not contribute to the core theoretical or experimental topics in the specified research directions.
motivation: Quantum simulation is limited by Hilbert space growth and software complexity, and the authors aim to reduce technical barriers by automating workflows.
method: The system uses multiple AI agents that reason over library documentation and APIs to translate natural-language scientific intent into executed and validated computations across various quantum software frameworks.
result: The system can assemble end-to-end simulations covering state preparation, dynamics, tensor networks, quantum control, error correction, and resource estimation, unifying different simulation paradigms behind a single interface.
conclusion: This approach opens a path toward scalable and autonomous quantum simulation, but it is primarily an AI/software engineering contribution rather than advancing quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: From Intuition To Optimization: A Review Of Inverse Design Applied To Optical Nanotweezers
authors: Sejeong Kim And Kenneth B Crozier Damian Nelson
abstract: Optical nanotweezers, which integrate nanophotonic structures such as plasmonic antennas, dielectric resonators, and metasurfaces, have emerged as powerful tools for manipulating nanoparticles, biomolecules, and viruses with high precision. However, traditional designs rely heavily on heuristic approaches and simple geometries, limiting performance. Inverse design offers a paradigm shift by using computational optimization methods to discover non-intuitive, high-performance structures for optical trapping. This review provides an overview of key inverse design methodologies, including adjoint-based optimization, topology optimization, and machine learning approaches, and highlights their broader impact across nanophotonics. We then focus on their application to optical nanotweezers, where recent advances demonstrate enhanced trapping stiffness, reduced optical heating, and tailored trapping landscapes. Representative examples include algorithmic design of plasmonic nanotweezers, topology-optimized plasmonic nanoapertures, inverse-designed dielectric nanocavities, and force-centric designs based on Maxwell stress tensor engineering. Collectively, these studies illustrate how inverse design enables stable, efficient, and versatile optical trapping at the nanoscale. Despite these advances, challenges remain in fabrication, computational cost, and the interpretability of optimized structures. We conclude with a perspective on future directions, emphasizing opportunities in reconfigurable tweezers, lab-on-a-chip integration, and quantum nanophotonics. By bridging photonic optimization with nanoscale manipulation, inverse-designed optical nanotweezers offer promising opportunities for future applications in biophysics, materials science, and quantum technologies.
tldr: A review of inverse design methods applied to optical nanotweezers, focusing on computational optimization for nanophotonic trapping structures.
motivation: Traditional optical nanotweezer designs rely on heuristics and simple geometries, limiting performance; inverse design offers a paradigm shift to discover high-performance structures.
method: The review surveys inverse design methodologies including adjoint-based optimization, topology optimization, and machine learning, and discusses their application to optical nanotweezers.
result: Recent advances demonstrate enhanced trapping stiffness, reduced optical heating, and tailored trapping landscapes, with examples like topology-optimized nanoapertures and inverse-designed nanocavities.
conclusion: Inverse-designed optical nanotweezers show promise for biophysics, materials science, and quantum technologies, but challenges remain in fabrication, computational cost, and interpretability.

title: Predissociation Dynamics Of Charged Long-range Rydberg Molecules
authors: Neethu Abraham, P. Giannakeas, Matthew T. Eiles
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate predissociation in homonuclear ([MATH]Rb[MATH][MATH]Rb[MATH]) and heteronuclear ([MATH]Rb[MATH][MATH]Li[MATH]) long-range Rydberg atom-ion molecules. Owing to their micron-scale bond lengths, these dissociate on time scales far removed from those of more tightly bound diatomic molecules. We employ the eigenchannel [MATH]-matrix method to compute predissociation rates for a broad range of principal quantum numbers [MATH]. The rates depend strongly on the mass, but more remarkably display a rapid and periodic variation as a function of [MATH] as well as within a single vibrational ladder. A semiclassical Landau-Zener-St\"uckelberg analysis reveals that St\"uckelberg interference governs the decay process and produces the observed variation in the molecular lifetime. Although the heavy mass of the homonuclear Rb molecule constrains its predissociation rates to a sub-kHz level, the lighter molecule [MATH]Rb[MATH][MATH]Li[MATH] dissociates on time scales competitive with radiative and collisional decay. This can enable in situ study of non-adiabatic decay via ion microscopy.
tldr: This paper studies predissociation dynamics of long-range Rydberg molecules, focusing on quantum interference effects in their decay rates.
motivation: Understanding the decay dynamics of long-range Rydberg molecules is important for their potential applications in quantum technologies, but the paper is primarily a molecular physics study.
method: The authors use the eigenchannel R-matrix method to compute predissociation rates and a semiclassical Landau-Zener-Stückelberg analysis to interpret the results.
result: They find that predissociation rates vary rapidly and periodically with principal quantum number and vibrational level, governed by Stückelberg interference, with lighter molecules dissociating faster.
conclusion: The study provides insights into non-adiabatic decay in Rydberg molecules, but it does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Identifiability-aware Neural Ordinary Differential Equations For Parsimonious And Reliable Dynamic Modelling
authors: Eva Balsa-Canto N\'uria Campo-Manzanares
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural ordinary differential equations (NODE) and hybrid NODE models provide flexible continuous-time representations of complex dynamic systems, but their expressive capacity can exceed the information content of the available data. Consequently, these models may reproduce observed trajectories while retaining weakly identifiable parameters, poorly constrained neural components, and unreliable extrapolation. Here we introduce identifiability-aware neural ordinary differential equations (iNODE), a framework that incorporates practical identifiability into neural differential equation design. iNODE models embed neural components as explicit analytic functions within the governing equations, enabling direct sensitivity analysis, Fisher-information-based confidence intervals, and identifiability-aware architecture selection. Candidate architectures are generated under data-support constraints, jointly calibrated, and ranked according to predictive accuracy, parsimony, and parameter identifiability. We evaluate the complete iNODE workflow against conventional NODE and hybrid NODE workflows representative of current practice using four controlled ground-truth benchmarks spanning fully data-driven and hybrid formulations, latent time-varying parameters, partial observability, and sparse or noisy measurements. Using the same training data and evaluation scenarios, the iNODE workflow selected more compact architectures, reduced parameter uncertainty, and improved extrapolation and recovery from latent-dynamics. These results establish practical identifiability as a model-design principle for parsimonious and reliable neural differential equations.
tldr: This paper introduces identifiability-aware neural ordinary differential equations (iNODE) for parsimonious and reliable dynamic modeling, focusing on parameter identifiability in hybrid neural differential equations.
motivation: Neural ODEs can overfit data and produce unreliable models due to weakly identifiable parameters and poorly constrained neural components.
method: iNODE embeds neural components as explicit analytic functions, enabling sensitivity analysis, Fisher-information-based confidence intervals, and identifiability-aware architecture selection under data-support constraints.
result: On four benchmarks, iNODE selected more compact architectures, reduced parameter uncertainty, and improved extrapolation and recovery from latent dynamics compared to conventional NODE workflows.
conclusion: Practical identifiability is established as a model-design principle for building parsimonious and reliable neural differential equations.
